questions.question: Determine the list price of an item if a 20% discount on the item amounts to Rs. 50.
questions.questionHtml: Determine the list price of an item if a 20% discount on the item amounts to Rs. 50.
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Discount% = 20 

Discount = Rs50 

FORMULA USED:

Discount% =  (Discount/M.P.) × 100 

Where, M.P. = Marked Price or list price 

CALCULATION:

Here, we have discount = Rs50  and discount% = 20 

⇒ Discount% = ( Discount/M.P.) × 100 

⇒ 20 = ( 50/M.P.) × 100 

⇒ M.P. = 250.

Hence, list price of an item is Rs250.

questions.solution:
SP after 20% discount: ₹1,500 - (0.20 × 1,500) = ₹1,200

questions.question: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 8%, 15% and 12% is:
questions.questionHtml: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 8%, 15% and 12% is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The successive discounts are 8%, 15% and 12%.

Concept used:

Using the concept of percentage.

Calculation:

Let the initial value be 100.

Discounted value = (100 – 8)% of (100 – 15)% of (100 – 12)% of 100

⇒ Discounted value = 92% of 85% of 88% of 100

⇒ Discounted value = 92/100 × 85/100 × 88/100 × 100

⇒ Discounted value = 68.816

Equivalent discount = (100 – Discounted value)/Initial value × 100

⇒ Equivalent discount = (100 – 68.816)/100 × 100

⇒ Equivalent discount = 31.184%

∴ A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts is 31.184%.

Alternate Method 8% = 8/100 = 2/25

15% = 15/100 = 3/20

12% = 12/100 = 3/25

8% 25 23
15% 20 17
12% 25 22
  25 × 20 × 25 23 × 17 × 22

25 × 20 × 25 = 12500

23 × 17 × 22 = 8602 

Discount % = \(\frac{12500-8602}{12500}\) × 100 = 389800/12500 = 31.184 %

 ∴ A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts is 31.184%. 

Shortcut Trick 

x + y -\(\frac{x \times y}{100}\)

8 + 15 - ​\(\frac{8 \times 15}{100}\)= 23 - 1.2 = 21.8​21.8 + 12 -\(\frac{21.8 \times 12}{100}\)= 33.8 - 2.616 = 31.184 %

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on the printed price of his goods and thus gains 20%. What is the ratio between the cost price and the printed price of the item?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on the printed price of his goods and thus gains 20%. What is the ratio between the cost price and the printed price of the item?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct ratio relation between Cost Price (CP) and Printed Price (MP):

CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

Given Discount = 10% and Profit = 20%

⇒ CP : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 20)

⇒ CP : MP = 90 : 120 = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Alternate Method

Given: Discount allowed = 10% | Profit earned = 20%

Formula Used: Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

⇒ Let the Printed Price (MP) of the item be ₹100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) after 10% discount = 100 − 10 = ₹90.

⇒ Since there is a 20% Profit, SP = CP × (120/100).

⇒ 90 = CP × (6/5)

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = (90 × 5) ÷ 6 = 15 × 5 = ₹75.

⇒ Ratio of CP to MP = 75 : 100

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4.

Additional Information

Direct CP and MP Relation

The relationship is derived as CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%). This is the fastest way to solve mark-up and discount problems.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It can also be calculated as [(Profit% + Discount%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d1 and d2 are given, the single equivalent discount is (d1 + d2 − d1×d2/100)%.

questions.question: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 6%, 15% and 14% is:
questions.questionHtml: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 6%, 15% and 14% is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Successive discount = 6%, 15% and 14%

Concept used:

S.P = M.P × (100 – D1)/100 × (100 – D2)/100 × (100 – D3)/100

Discount = M.P – S.P 

Discount% = ((Discount)/(M.P)) × 100

Calcualtions:

Let MP be 100x

⇒ S.P = 100x × (100 – 6)/100 × (100 – 15)/100 × (100 – 14)/100

⇒ (100x × 94 × 85 × 86)/100 × 100 × 100)

⇒ 68.714x

Discount = 100x – 68.714x = 31.286x

Discount% = (31.286x/100x) × 100 = 31.286%

∴ The equivalent discount% is 31.286%

Alternate Method Let MP be 100x

⇒ S.P = 100x × (100 – 6)/100 × (100 – 15)/100 × (100 – 14)/100

⇒ (100x × 94 × 85 × 86)/100 × 100 × 100)

⇒ 68.714x

Discount = 100x – 68.714x = 31.286x

Discount% = (31.286x/100x) × 100 = 31.286%

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 600. A shopkeeper purchased it on two successive discounts of 10% and 20%. He spent Rs. 68 on transportation and sold the article for Rs. 600. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 600. A shopkeeper purchased it on two successive discounts of 10% and 20%. He spent Rs. 68 on transportation and sold the article for Rs. 600. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
MP = Rs. 600, Successive Discounts = 10% and 20%

Transportation = Rs. 68, SP = Rs. 600

Effective Discount = 10% + 20% - (10% × 20%) / 100 = 28%

CP after discount = MP - (28 / 100) × 600 = 600 - 168 = 432

Total CP = 432 + 68 = 500

Gain = SP - Total CP = 600 - 500 = 100

Gain% = (100 / 500) × 100 = 20%

Final Discount% = (A + B) - (AB/100) = (25 + 8) - [(25 × 8)/100] = 31%

Selling Price = MP(1 - D%) =  2500(1 - 31%) = Rs. 1725

questions.question: A merchant allows a discount of 20 percent on marked price. If he wants to earn a profit of 20 percent, then marked price will be how much percentage more than the cost price?
questions.questionHtml: A merchant allows a discount of 20 percent on marked price. If he wants to earn a profit of 20 percent, then marked price will be how much percentage more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
SP = CP + Profit = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120

SP after discount = 80 % of MP

120 = 80 % of the MP

MP = 120/0.8 = 150

MP more than CP = (150 - 100)/100 × 100 = 50%

questions.question: An item with a marked price of ₹z was sold for ₹6,622, after a discount of 12% was offered. What was the value of z?
questions.questionHtml: An item with a marked price of ₹z was sold for ₹6,622, after a discount of 12% was offered. What was the value of z?
questions.solution:
Selling Price = Marked Price (1 - \(\frac{D}{100}\) ) 

⇒ 6622 = z ( 1 - \(\frac{12}{100}\) ) ⇒ 6622 = z (88/100)  ⇒ z = (6622 x 100/ 88)  ⇒ z = ₹ 7,525

questions.question: In a grocery store, an item with an MRP of Rs 1,000 is on a discount counter with a special prices of Rs 979. What is the percentage of discount given for that item?
questions.questionHtml: In a grocery store, an item with an MRP of Rs 1,000 is on a discount counter with a special prices of Rs 979. What is the percentage of discount given for that item?
questions.solution:
Formula Used-

Discount % = (MRP - Discounted Price)/MRP × 100

Calculation- 

Discount % = (1000 - 979)/1000 × 100

⇒ 2.1

∴ Percentage of discount given for that item = 2.1%

questions.question: At a factory outlet of a footwear company, every item is available at a discount of 10%. Charu selected footwear marked for Rs. 900. While paying the bill, it was found that the footwear was slightly damaged for which she got another discount of 10%. How much did she pay for the footwear?
questions.questionHtml: At a factory outlet of a footwear company, every item is available at a discount of 10%. Charu selected footwear marked for Rs. 900. While paying the bill, it was found that the footwear was slightly damaged for which she got another discount of 10%. How much did she pay for the footwear?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price of footwear = Rs. 900

Concept used:

Successive discount

Calculation:

According to the question,

CP of footwear at which Charu brought that = 900 × 9/10 × 9/10

⇒ 9 × 9 × 9

⇒ Rs. 729

∴ She paid Rs. 729 for the footwear.

Alternate Method-10% -10% + (-10 × -10)/100

⇒ - 20% + 1%

⇒ - 19%

⇒ Actual discount = - 19%

So, CP = 900 × 81/100

⇒ Rs. 729

∴ She paid Rs. 729 for the footwear.

questions.question: Rakhi purchased a basket, a wallet and a belt. She got discounts of 5%, 8% and 10% on the basket, the wallet and the belt, respectively, on their respective marked prices of ₹80, ₹150 and ₹350. How much amount (in ₹) did she pay in total?
questions.questionHtml: Rakhi purchased a basket, a wallet and a belt. She got discounts of 5%, 8% and 10% on the basket, the wallet and the belt, respectively, on their respective marked prices of ₹80, ₹150 and ₹350. How much amount (in ₹) did she pay in total?
questions.solution:
For the basket:

Discount amount = (80 × 5/100 = ₹4) ⇒ Discounted price = (80 - 4 = ₹76)

 

For the wallet:

Discount amount = (150 × 8/100 = ₹12) ⇒ Discounted price = (150 - 12 = ₹138)

For the belt:

Discount amount = (350 × 10/100 = ₹35) ⇒ Discounted price = (350 - 35 = ₹315)

⇒ Total = (76 + 138 + 315 = ₹529)

questions.question: Sujatha sold 75% of her goods at a profit of 24% and the remaining at a loss of 40%. What is her gain/loss percentage on the whole transaction?
questions.questionHtml: Sujatha sold 75% of her goods at a profit of 24% and the remaining at a loss of 40%. What is her gain/loss percentage on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
As we know, 75% = 3/4

Let total goods be 400 and their cost price also be 400.

SP of the 300 goods = 300 × (124/100) = 372

SP of the 100 goods = 100 × (60/100) = 60

Total SP of the goods = 372 + 60 = 432

Profit percentage = [(432 – 400)/400] × 100 = 8%
